supplier_interface.text: Let $(P^{2n},\omega)$ be symplectic, and let $N=\{\chi_1=\cdots=\chi_r=0\}$ be a regular embedded level surface with $\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}=0$ on $N$. Then $\ker(\omega|_N)$ is exactly the rank-$r$ distribution spanned by the restricted Hamiltonian vector fields $X_{\chi_a}$. This distribution is involutive. Around every point of $N$, its leaves admit smooth Frobenius coordinates $(s^1,\ldots,s^r,y^1,\ldots,y^{2n-2r})$, and the local leaf space has a unique smooth closed nondegenerate two-form $\omega_{\mathrm{red}}$ whose pullback is $\omega|_N$. Thus regular first-class constraints yield a local symplectic quotient. No global orbit-space regularity follows from these hypotheses.

rationale: Actual supplier supplies the local mathematical theorem used in the witness argument.

supplier_interface.text: For dependent deductions, the adopted premise is that on a finite fixed-endpoint timelike segment in a local potential domain, the model trajectory is stationary for the displayed action. The potential and metric are fixed inputs, $m>0$ and $q$ are constant, and this premise asserts neither a global potential nor global trajectory existence.

rationale: Supplier supplies the quantities/conventions needed to formulate this independent adopted premise; it does not derive the postulate.

supplier_interface.text:
Adopt as physical assumptions of the special-relativity framework the following
two statements, with the SI coordinate and unit conventions of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]].

**(i) Ideal clocks.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nondegenerate interval and
$\gamma:I\to A$ a curve. Choose an inertial chart $\chi$ with
$E(u)=\sum_au^ae_a$ as in [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]. Require
$y:=\chi\circ\gamma:I\to\mathbb R^4$ to be $C^1$ on the interior of $I$,
with its derivative extending continuously to any included endpoints, where
it is the one-sided derivative. Define the displacement-valued derivative by
$\dot\gamma(s):=E(y'(s))\in V$ and require $\dot\gamma(s)\in C^+$ everywhere,
including such endpoints. This derivative is chart-independent: a second
chart has coordinates $\widetilde y=M^{-1}(y-\chi(o'))$, so its
parameter derivative is $M^{-1}\mathrm dy/\mathrm ds$, while its basis map
is $E'=EM$; their product is $E\,\mathrm dy/\mathrm ds$.

An **ideal clock on this curve** has a reading map $\sigma:I\to\mathbb R$
in seconds, specified up to an additive constant, with, for all $a<b$ in $I$,

$$\sigma(b)-\sigma(a)=c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta\bigl(\dot\gamma(s),\dot\gamma(s)\bigr)}\,\mathrm ds .$$

The integrand is positive and continuous on $[a,b]$: the coordinate derivatives
are continuous, $\eta$ is a finite bilinear expression, and the square root
is continuous at every positive argument, as follows from
$|\sqrt r-\sqrt q|=|r-q|/(\sqrt r+\sqrt q)$ for $r,q>0$.
Thus [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]] applies to this compact interval
and gives a well-defined Riemann integral. The reading rule contains no
additional acceleration-dependent correction (**clock hypothesis**); it does
not require $C^2$ regularity or an acceleration to exist. This is an adopted
physical interpretation of the length integral, not a proof about real clocks.

**(ii) Ideal light.** In vacuum, the **ideal light rays** are the oriented
straight lines parametrized by $\ell:\mathbb R\to A$,
$\ell(\lambda)=p+\lambda v$, where $p\in A$ and $v\in V$ is future null;
increasing $\lambda$ specifies their future direction. In an inertial chart
$\chi$ their coordinate map is

$$\chi(\ell(\lambda))=\chi(p)+\lambda\,(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3).$$

Since the chart's time-axis vector is future, the cone description of
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] gives
$v^0=\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert>0$. With $t=\chi^0/c$ the spatial
coordinate velocity is $c(v^1,v^2,v^3)/v^0$ and has Euclidean magnitude $c$
in every inertial chart. The conversion constant is the same across charts;
its exact SI numerical value is a unit convention as specified in
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], while the ideal-vacuum-light
interpretation is an adopted, empirically testable model assumption.

rationale: Supplier supplies the quantities/conventions needed to formulate this independent adopted premise; it does not derive the postulate.

supplier_interface.text:
Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units $[F]$ and $[G]$ has units $[F][G]/(\text{action})$. These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

rationale: Supplier supplies the quantities/conventions needed to formulate this independent adopted premise; it does not derive the postulate.

supplier_interface.text:
Adopt as physical assumptions of the relativistic particle model, on top of the
flat spacetime model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and the SI unit
conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], together with
the framework's idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks and ideal light
signals:

**(i) Mass and momentum.** Every massive classical particle of the model
carries a positive constant invariant mass parameter $m>0$ and has
four-momentum $P=mU$, where $U$ is the four-velocity of its future timelike
worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]],
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]); $P$ is a vector of $V$
whose SI unit is kilogram metre per second. The formula is adopted only for
$m>0$; the case $m=0$ is not defined by it and is the separate premise
[[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. In particular $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$
is a consequence of the four-velocity normalisation, not a separate
assumption.

**(ii) Observer measurement identification.** Relative to a future unit
observer $n$, the model identifies the measured energy of the particle with
$E_n(P)$, its measured spatial momentum with $q_n(P)$, its kinetic energy with
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and its rest energy with $mc^2$, where $E_n,q_n,T_n$ are
the quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; the
units are the joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. This clause is a formulation
convention identifying mathematical quantities with the quantities the model
calls measured; it is not a measurement report and no experiment is claimed.

**(iii) Isolated collision balance.** An isolated collision is represented by
a mass-specified on-shell collision datum at an event, with finite nonempty
incoming and outgoing lists of the massive particles of (i) and/or the ideal
massless particles of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]], and with
no external four-momentum transfer or omitted leg. The interaction is
idealized as confined to that event. The sum of the incoming four-momenta equals the sum of the
outgoing four-momenta, in the sense of the collision data of
[[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]: the model adopts
$Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$ for such an isolated datum. No particular
collision is asserted to occur, and no mechanism, probability, cross section
or amplitude is supplied by this clause.

**(iv) Equation of motion for a stipulated force.** Put
$H_c^+:=\{U\in C^+:\eta(U,U)=-c^2\}$. A stipulated force law is a given
map $F:D\to V$ on a given subset $D\subseteq A\times H_c^+$,
with force components in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m/\mathrm s^2$. No regularity
away from the specified worldline is assumed. Along a given $C^2$ massive worldline
$x:I\to A$ with $(x(s),U(s))\in D$ for all $s\in I$, the model's particle
equation is $m\,dU/d\tau=F(x,U)$, with
$dU/d\tau$ the proper-time derivative of
[[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]], so that the stipulated $F$
is the four-force of the motion. A particular force law, and the existence,
uniqueness and domain of solutions of the resulting equation, are not adopted
here and belong to a separate model.

Empirical support for these assumptions is a nonlogical relation of the
framework, not a proof; the idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks,
ideal light signals and flat spacetime are inherited and travel to every
consumer of this premise.

rationale: Supplier supplies the quantities/conventions needed to formulate this independent adopted premise; it does not derive the postulate.

supplier_interface.text:
**Adopted convention.** On a prescribed background $(M,g,N)$ from [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]], an ideal clock carried along a future timelike test worldline $x$ records the proper-time parameter $\tau$ defined by $d\tau=c^{-1}\sqrt{-g(dx/ds,dx/ds)}\,ds$. Thus elapsed reading between two ordered points is the integral of this positive density. The flat-spacetime specialization is inherited from [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]; extending that convention to the curved prescribed background is a separate adoption of this framework.

When the parameter $s$ is measured in seconds, $x^0=ct$ is in metres, $c$ is in metres per second, and $\tau$ is in seconds. This is a model postulate, not a theorem or a reported measurement. It does not assert that a physical clock realizes the idealization exactly, that the background solves gravitational field equations, or that the test body affects the background.

supplier_interface.text:
Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region
$U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart $x$ of the framework
([[def-em-lab-geometry]]), $k\ge1$, with the SI units of
[[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components
$F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$,
$F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$,
$v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $\Lambda_\beta$ be the explicit boost of
[[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]] with
$\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_0=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_1=\gamma$,
$\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_1=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$,
$\Lambda_\beta{}^2{}_2=\Lambda_\beta{}^3{}_3=1$ and all other entries zero. Let
$x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the corresponding inertial chart, and for every event
$p$ in the overlap of the two chart restrictions define the primed field
components by reading the components of the same $F$ in $x'$ through the
dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], so that $F'_{0i}=-E'_i/c$,
$F'_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B'_k$ at $p$. Then:

(a) [Boosted fields] at every such $p$, with $\parallel$ and $\perp$ the
components along and orthogonal to $e_1$ in the spatial Euclidean structure of
the chart,
$$E'_1=E_1,\quad B'_1=B_1,\qquad E'_\parallel=E_\parallel,\quad B'_\parallel=B_\parallel,\qquad E'_\perp=\gamma\,(E+v\times B)_\perp,\qquad B'_\perp=\gamma\,(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp,$$
equivalently, componentwise,
$E'_2=\gamma(E_2-\beta cB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+\beta cB_2)$,
$B'_2=\gamma(B_2+\beta E_3/c)$, $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$.

(a′) [Arbitrary boost direction] For a velocity vector $v\in\mathbb R^3$ with
$|v|<c$, use the actual vector boost $B(v/c)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]], with
$\gamma_v=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. If $v\ne0$, decompose the fields along
$\widehat v=v/|v|$ and its orthogonal complement. Then $E'_\parallel=E_\parallel$,
$B'_\parallel=B_\parallel$, $E'_\perp=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and
$B'_\perp=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$. Equivalently, for every $v$,
including $v=0$,
$$E'=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot E)}{c^2},\qquad B'=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot B)}{c^2}.$$
At $v=0$ these are the identity and no preferred parallel direction is
assigned.

(b) [Invariants] at every such $p$,
$$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=E\cdot B;$$
equivalently the scalar fields $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$
and $I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,E\cdot B/c$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]
(b) take the same values whether computed from the components in $x$ or in
$x'$.

(c) [General proper orthochronous changes] for any proper orthochronous Lorentz
matrix $\Lambda$ with chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$, the primed components of $F$ are
given by the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii),
$F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$; in particular, if
$\Lambda=\widehat R$ is the extension of a spatial rotation $R$ of the frame
([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]), then $E'=RE$ and $B'=RB$, and
by the unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of
[[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii) every proper
orthochronous change acts first by $(E,B)\mapsto(RE,RB)$ and then by the
arbitrary-direction boost law (a′) with velocity $-c\beta$, where $\beta$ is
the vector parameter of that factorization. The axis-only law (a) is not
substituted for a general vector boost.

(d) [Form invariance of the Maxwell branch] if $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfy the
smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] in $x$ on the overlap, and
$(\rho',J')$ are the components of the same four-current in $x'$, then
$(E',B',\rho',J')$ satisfy the same four equations in $x'$, by
[[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]].

(e) [Scope] All clauses are pointwise on the overlap $U\cap U'$ of the two
chart restrictions, are conditional on the adopted postulates, and concern the
smooth classical flat branch; no accelerating coordinates, curved spacetime,
material medium, apparatus or empirical claim is involved; the transformation
is exact algebra, and the primed component functions are $C^k$ wherever the
overlap is open. The invariants clause uses only the proper orthochronous
changes of description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]];
orientation-reversing changes are outside the framework's field conventions
([[def-em-fields]]).

rationale: Actual supplier is a conditional physics theorem; the consumer uses its established model result with its qualifications.

supplier_interface.text:
Let $c>0$ and let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike worldline in the affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]), with generic parameter $s\in I$. Write $\tau:I\to\tau[I]$ for its proper-time function and $U(s):=x'(s)/\tau'(s)$, $A(s):=U'(s)/\tau'(s)$ for its four-velocity and four-acceleration ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]). These are proper-time derivatives evaluated at the event $x(s)$; $s$ need not itself be proper time. Pointwise $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, $\eta(U,A)=0$, and $A(s)$ is spacelike whenever it is nonzero ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a),(b)).

**(a) Definition.** The **proper acceleration** of $x$ at the parameter value $s$ is the real number

$$a(s) := \sqrt{\eta(A(s),A(s))},$$

the nonnegative square root of [[def-rational-power]]. This is well defined for every $s \in I$. Indeed, fix an inertial chart of $A$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]); since $x$ is $C^2$, the component functions of $A$ are continuous, and $\eta(A,A)$ is a sum of products of continuous component functions, hence continuous, by [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]]. If $A(s) = 0$ then $\eta(A,A) = 0$ at $s$, and if $A(s) \neq 0$ then $A(s)$ is spacelike and $\eta(A,A) > 0$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); in both cases the argument of the square root is nonnegative, so $a(s)$ is a well-defined nonnegative real number for every $s \in I$. With the SI coordinate and unit conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], in which $x^0 = c t$ with $t$ in seconds and the spatial coordinates are in metres while $\eta$ has the dimensionless matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ in an inertial chart, the components of $A$ carry the unit metre per second squared and $\eta(A,A)$ carries the unit $(\text{metre per second squared})^2$, so $a$ carries the unit metre per second squared. The worldline is **uniformly accelerated** when $a$ is constant on $I$.

**(b) Agreement with the acceleration of a congruence.** Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset of $A$ and let $n : \Omega \to V$ be an observer congruence with acceleration field $a_{\mathrm{cg}} := \nabla_n n$, where $\nabla$ is the flat covariant derivative of [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (b)). If $x$ is a flow line of $n$ and $U = c n$ along $x$, then $A = c^2 a_{\mathrm{cg}}$ along $x$: the derivative along the worldline of the field $n$ is the covariant derivative $\nabla_{dx/d\tau} n = \nabla_{cn} n = c \nabla_n n = c\, a_{\mathrm{cg}}$, by the defining properties of the flat covariant derivative along curves ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] (d)), so $A = d(c n)/d\tau = c\, \nabla_{dx/d\tau} n = c^2 a_{\mathrm{cg}}$. Consequently $a = c^2 \sqrt{\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})}$ along $x$: the proper acceleration is $c^2$ times the magnitude of the congruence acceleration. In particular the proper acceleration of a congruence worldline is determined by the congruence field alone, and such a worldline is uniformly accelerated exactly when $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})$ is constant along it.

**(c) Reading and scope.** This item defines a quantity of the model and fixes its name, its unit and its physical reading. The model reads $a(s)$ as the magnitude that an ideal accelerometer carried along the worldline would register at $s$; this ideal-instrument identification is adopted with the model in the same sense as the framework's ideal-clock reading of proper time and is not derived here. No accelerometer response law, calibration, frequency dependence, force law or interaction is specified or asserted; the definition asserts nothing about which bodies follow which worldlines; no measurement outcome and no statistical, uncertainty or empirical claim is made. No choice principle is used.

rationale: Physical definition supplies model quantities/ideal measurement meaning used to formulate this conditional physical result.

supplier_interface.text:
Adopt [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and [[post-sr-causal-signal-propagation]], and the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] ($x^0 = c t$). Let $x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be the chart of an inertial frame ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) and let $W := \{x^1 > |x^0|\}$ be the right wedge. Let $\Phi$ and $n$ be the Rindler chart and congruence of [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (b): $\Phi(\theta,\rho,y,z) = (\rho \sinh \theta, \rho \cosh \theta, y, z)$ on $\mathbb R \times (0,\infty) \times \mathbb R^2$ with inverse $\rho = \sqrt{(x^1)^2 - (x^0)^2}$, $\theta = \frac12 \log((x^1+x^0)/(x^1-x^0))$, pullback metric $-\rho^2 d\theta^2 + d\rho^2 + dy^2 + dz^2$, and acceleration field $a_{\mathrm{cg}} = \nabla_n n = \rho^{-1} \partial_\rho$. Fix $\rho_0 > 0$ and real $y_0,z_0$, and let $O$ be the congruence worldline $\rho = \rho_0$, $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$, parametrized by its proper time $\tau$ with $\theta = c \tau/\rho_0$; by [[def-sr-proper-acceleration]] its proper acceleration is $c^2/\rho_0$. Write $U(q) := q^0 + q^1$ and $V(q) := q^0 - q^1$ for events $q$, so that $U = \rho e^{\theta}$ and $V = -\rho e^{-\theta}$ on $W$, and write $\le$ and $J^+$, $J^-$ for the causal reachability relations of [[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]]. Then, conditionally on the adopted model:

(i) **Chart domain and light rays.** $\Phi$ is a smooth bijection of $\mathbb R \times (0,\infty) \times \mathbb R^2$ onto $W$ with the stated smooth inverse, so the chart domain is exactly $W$ and $\rho = 0$ is not part of its coordinate domain. The boundary of $W$ in the affine model is $\{x^1 = |x^0|\}$, with arbitrary $x^2,x^3$: it is the union of the two null half-planes $\{x^1 = x^0 \ge 0\}$ and $\{x^1 = -x^0 \ge 0\}$. These half-planes are portions of the full null planes appearing as causal horizons in (ii); the full planes are not the wedge boundary. Along the worldline $\rho = \rho_0$ one has $V = -\rho_0 e^{-\theta} \to 0^-$ and $U \to +\infty$ as $\theta \to +\infty$, while $U = \rho_0 e^{\theta} \to 0^+$ and $V \to -\infty$ as $\theta \to -\infty$. The future null straight lines of the model that lie in the plane $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$ and meet $O$ are exactly the lines of constant $V$ (on which $d\theta = +d\rho/\rho$) and the lines of constant $U$ (on which $d\theta = -d\rho/\rho$).

(ii) **Causal horizons.** An event $q$ satisfies $q \le p$ for some event $p$ of $O$ if and only if $V(q) < 0$; an event $q$ satisfies $p \le q$ for some event $p$ of $O$ if and only if $U(q) > 0$. Consequently no event with $V(q) \ge 0$ can ever influence $O$; this set contains the null plane $\{x^1 = x^0\}$, the left wedge $\{x^1 < -|x^0|\}$ and the future wedge $\{x^0 > |x^1|\}$; and no event with $U(q) \le 0$ can ever be influenced by $O$, a set containing the null plane $\{x^1 = -x^0\}$, the left wedge and the past wedge $\{x^0 < -|x^1|\}$. The null plane $\{x^1 = x^0\}$ is the boundary of the causal past of $O$ (the future horizon: the surface its worldline approaches as $\theta \to +\infty$), and the null plane $\{x^1 = -x^0\}$ is the boundary of the causal future of $O$ (the past horizon); every event of the left wedge is causally unrelated to $O$ in both directions. The same criteria with $O$ any other congruence worldline $\rho = \rho_1$, $y = y_1$, $z = z_1$ hold verbatim: the constants $\rho_0$, $y_0$, $z_0$ do not enter.

(iii) **Radar time and distance to a coaxial congruence reflector.** Fix $\rho_m > 0$ with $\rho_m \ne \rho_0$ and let $R_m$ be the congruence worldline $\rho = \rho_m$, $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$ (a second uniformly accelerated observer, coaxial with $O$, with proper acceleration $c^2/\rho_m$). Let $e_-$ be the event of $O$ at parameter $\theta_e$ (so $\tau(e_-) = \rho_0 \theta_e/c$ up to the base point of $\tau$), let $q_m$ be the event of $R_m$ lying on the future null straight line from $e_-$ in the plane $y = y_0$, $z = z_0$, and let $e_+$ be the event of $O$ lying on the future null straight line from $q_m$; the reflection at $q_m$ is idealized as instantaneous and as leaving $R_m$'s motion unchanged, as in [[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]]. Then $e_-, q_m, e_+$ exist uniquely, the Rindler time of $q_m$ is $\theta_m = \theta_e + |\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$, the return event satisfies $\theta(e_+) = \theta_e + 2|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ and $(\theta_e + \theta(e_+))/2 = \theta_m$, so the round trip lasts $2|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ in Rindler time and $(2\rho_0/c)|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ in $O$'s proper time. For every distinct positive reflector radius the notions differ: with $r = \rho_m/\rho_0$, one has $\log r < r - 1$ when $r > 1$ and $-\log r > 1 - r$ when $0 < r < 1$. The two distance formulas agree only at $r = 1$, where both have the continuous degenerate value zero. The coincident case is not a nonzero emission-reflection-reception triple of the protocol, whose distinct-reflector hypothesis remains in force. As $\rho_m \to 0^+$ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration $c^2/\rho_m$ diverges; as $\rho_m \to +\infty$ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance also grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration tends to $0$.

(iv) **Restrictions of the protocol.** No event with $V \ge 0$ --- in particular no event of the horizon plane $\{x^1 = x^0\}$, of the left wedge or of the future wedge --- can be assigned a radar time or radar distance by this protocol from $O$, because by (ii) it cannot causally precede any reception event on $O$: the required reflection-to-reception leg is impossible. Separately, every event with $U \le 0$ lacks an emission-to-reflection leg from $O$. Thus any event admitting this radar triple must satisfy $U > 0$ and $V < 0$, equivalently it must belong to $W$; the horizon is at infinite radar distance in the limit $\rho_m \to 0^+$. For example $q = x^{-1}(2\rho_0,0,y_0,z_0)$ has $U(q) = V(q) = 2\rho_0 > 0$. It is causally after $O$ at $\theta = 0$, since the displacement is $(2\rho_0,-\rho_0,0,0)$, future timelike, and it even lies on a future null ray from $O$ at $\theta = \log 2$, with displacement $(5\rho_0/4,-5\rho_0/4,0,0)$. Nevertheless it cannot send a causal return to $O$, so it receives no radar assignment from $O$. The protocol therefore does not extend to a global coordinate system of $A$.

(v) **Scope.** All clauses are conditional computations and readings in flat classical spacetime with ideal clocks, ideal light rays and ideal reflectors, for the specified congruence worldlines. They are not empirical claims and contain no measurement, apparatus, source, detector or statistical content; gravitation, media, dispersion, finite resolution, quantum effects and material models of the reflector are excluded. No choice principle is used.

supplier_interface.text:
Adopt the postulates [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]],
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]],
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] and
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] of the classical gravitational
framework, with the field law in its direct-equation presentation and the unit
conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let
$(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum of mass parameter $m_*>0$ with
Schwarzschild radius $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ and static congruence
$n=f^{-1/2}\partial_0$, $f(r)=1-s/r$
([[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]]), and let the model's stress-energy
tensor be the vacuum prescription

$$T:=0\qquad\text{on }M,\qquad \Lambda:=0 .$$

Then all statements below are conditional deductions inside the model so
specified; they assert nothing about nature.

**(a) The Schwarzschild vacuum model.** $(M,g,N)$ satisfies the spacetime
postulate, $T=0$ is a smooth symmetric stress-energy tensor field on the
matter domain $M$ in the sense of [[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]], the
prescription is admissible, and the adopted field law
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ holds identically on $M$. A **vacuum solution with zero cosmological parameter** here means
precisely a datum satisfying that equation with $T=0$ and $\Lambda=0$;
this datum is such a solution, read as a model of the framework. The model is not locally flat: its curvature tensor is nowhere
zero, while its Ricci tensor and Einstein tensor vanish identically
([[lem-gr-schwarzschild-ricci-and-einstein-tensors]] clause (d)).

**(b) Static clock readings.** The integral curves of $n$ are the static
observer worldlines at constant radius $r_0$
([[lem-gr-schwarzschild-static-congruence-and-clock-rates]] clause (b));
adopting the clock rule of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] clause (i),
the reading difference of an ideal clock carried along such a worldline
between two events whose coordinate times differ by $\Delta t$ is

$$\Delta\tau=\sqrt{f(r_0)}\,\Delta t=\sqrt{1-\frac{s}{r_0}}\;\Delta t,$$

so two static clocks at radii $r_1,r_2$ compared over the same coordinate
interval with $\Delta t\ne0$ satisfy $\Delta\tau_1/\Delta\tau_2=\sqrt{f(r_1)/f(r_2)}$. The static
worldlines are not geodesics: their acceleration is
$a=\frac{s}{2r^2}\partial_r\ne0$, so the model assigns them to accelerated
(constrained) bodies and not to freely falling ones.

**(c) The mass parameter.** The parameter $m_*$ enters the model only through
$s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$ and through the quantities below; the framework reads $m_*$ as
the mass parameter of the model in kilograms
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]] clause (a),
[[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]] clause (a)):

1. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a smooth future timelike geodesic, parametrized
   by proper time $\tau$ on an interval with nonempty interior, with
   $r\circ\gamma\equiv r_0>\frac{3s}{2}$. Put $\sigma:=\iota\circ\gamma:I\to S^2$
   and $t:=(x^0\circ\gamma)/c$. Its **angular speed with respect to $t$** is
   $\Omega:=\sqrt{\gamma_{S^2}(d\sigma/dt,d\sigma/dt)}$, where
   $d\sigma/dt:=\sigma'(\tau)/t'(\tau)$ and $t'(\tau)>0$ by future
   timelikeness. It has units $\mathrm s^{-1}$ and satisfies
   $\Omega^2=G_Nm_*/r_0^3$ in every angular orientation. For an equatorial
   curve, $\vartheta=\pi/2$ and $\Omega^2=(d\varphi/dt)^2$ in local polar
   charts ([[lem-gr-schwarzschild-circular-orbits-and-photon-sphere]]
   clause (a) and proof step 2.2). This is the Kepler-like law in which
   $m_*$ plays the role of the central mass;
2. in the isotropic chart of
   [[lem-gr-schwarzschild-isotropic-coordinate-form]], with
   $a=s/(4\rho)$, the exact identity
   $g_{00}+1=1-\bigl((1-a)/(1+a)\bigr)^2=4a/(1+a)^2$ gives
   $$g_{00}+1=+\frac{s}{\rho}+O(\rho^{-2})=+\frac{2G_Nm_*}{c^2\rho}+O(\rho^{-2}).$$
   Under the weak-field convention $g_{00}=-(1+2\Phi/c^2)$ to leading order
   ([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]]), this is the coefficient
   $-2\Phi_N/c^2$ for the explicit exterior Newtonian potential
   $\Phi_N(\rho):=-G_Nm_*/\rho$ in the comparison reading of
   [[def-gr-newtonian-comparison-model-and-identification]].

The reading is a statement about the model's own identities and the adopted
unit and weak-field conventions; no numerical value of $G_N$ or $m_*$, no
Newtonian source model realized by matter and no comparison with any reported
mass is asserted.

**(d) Scope.** The model is an idealized vacuum model of the framework, not a
claim about the actual universe: no observation, apparatus, calibration or
uncertainty is used, and no comparison with data is made. The datum solves the
field law with the chosen parameters $(m_*,\Lambda,T)=(m_*,0,0)$; other
solutions of the same field law exist and are not excluded, and the exterior
domain $r>s$ contains no horizon or interior region, whose treatment is the
subject of the extension and Kruskal items of this page. The physical
interpretation of coordinates, clocks and bodies remains the adopted one of
the cited postulates.
